prompt.context: Your client works in financial services in the arbitrage business, which is quite lucrative. It has no profitability problem and no competition. The company has 4 senior analysts, 3 junior analysts, and 1 admin. The activities in which they are involved include the initial stage (20% of the work), the core stage (70% of the work), and the recommendation (10% of the work). These percentages are constant.
prompt.question: How many junior analysts need to be added to free up capacity among the senior analysts, so they can focus on selling additional work?

clarifying_info.q: How much of each activity are the different staff types engaged in?
clarifying_info.a: Senior Analysts do 60% initial, 20% core, and 80% recommendations. Junior analysts do 30% initial, 70% core, and 20% recommendations. Admin does 10% initial and 10% core, with no recommendations.

framework: Determine the share of total firm work currently done by junior analysts across all three activity stages
Calculate how much work each junior analyst carries individually (share / number of junior analysts)
Determine how many junior analysts are needed for junior analysts to collectively handle 100% of the workload they are responsible for
Subtract current junior analyst headcount to find the number of additional hires needed
Identify the new binding constraint after headcount is expanded

questions.prompt: What percentage of total firm work is currently being performed by junior analysts?
questions.guidance: Multiply each activity's share of total work by the junior analyst contribution to that activity, then sum across all three stages.

math.setup: Activity weights: Initial=20%, Core=70%, Recommendation=10%. Junior analyst contributions: 30% of Initial, 70% of Core, 20% of Recommendations.
math.answer: Junior analysts collectively handle 57% of total firm work.

questions.prompt: How much work is each junior analyst currently doing? How many junior analysts are needed to reach 100% capacity?
questions.guidance: Divide the total junior analyst share by the current number of junior analysts to get per-analyst load, then scale up to 100%.

steps: Per analyst load = 57% / 3 = 19% of total firm work
math.answer: 2 additional junior analysts need to be hired.

questions.prompt: Once five junior analysts are in place, what is the new constraint on getting the work done?
questions.guidance: With headcount no longer the bottleneck, the binding constraint shifts to time — the hours available to complete the work.

recommendation: Hire 2 additional junior analysts to bring the junior analyst team to 5, fully absorbing the workload they are equipped to handle and freeing senior analysts to focus on business development.
risks: Ramp-up time for new junior analysts may temporarily reduce throughput
Time becomes the new constraint once headcount is resolved — workflow and scheduling processes should be reviewed
next_steps: Review time allocation and scheduling to address the newly binding time constraint
Monitor senior analyst capacity to confirm they can redirect effort toward selling additional work
